input.dimension: Process-level and encoding behaviour (argv byte decoding, locale/env, fd & pipe failure modes, stdin, exit codes)

findings.rule: Baseline. Both lines are emitted as ONE 8192-byte-buffered write() flushed at interpreter exit (verified via Node spawn: exactly one 'data' chunk of "True\nTrue\n"). stdout is block-buffered when piped/redirected, line-buffered on a TTY; the final byte stream is identical either way. Terminator is always LF (0x0A), never CRLF — CRLF seen under script(1) is the pty's ONLCR, not the program.

Invalid UTF-8 in --key NEVER crashes. argv bytes are decoded UTF-8 + PEP-383 surrogateescape, so 0xFF becomes U+DCFF; the resulting 1-char string simply isn't a bidict key, so result1=False. No traceback, rc=0.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '\\udcff'\n
findings.rule: THE headline case. Invalid UTF-8 in --val surfaces as the LITERAL 7-byte text \udcff (backslash,u,d,c,f,f) inside the argparse repr. Byte 0xNN -> the six characters \udcNN with NN lowercase hex. Two independent mechanisms both produce this: (a) Python repr() escapes lone surrogates as \udcXX, and (b) sys.stderr's default errors='backslashreplace' would escape them anyway. stdout is EMPTY.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '\\udcff\\udcfe'\n
findings.rule: surrogateescape is PER BYTE, not per maximal-subpart: every individual undecodable byte gets its own U+DC00+byte. No U+FFFD ever appears. JS TextDecoder(non-fatal) gives one U+FFFD per subpart and is therefore WRONG.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '\\udced\\udca0\\udc80'\n
findings.rule: UTF-8-encoded surrogates (CESU-8 style, ED A0 80 = U+D800) are INVALID for Python's decoder -> 3 escapes. Same for ED BF BF -> '\udced\udcbf\udcbf'.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '\\udcc0\\udc80'\n
findings.rule: Overlong encodings are rejected byte-by-byte. Verified family: C0 80, C1 BF, E0 80 80 -> '\udce0\udc80\udc80', F0 82 82 AC -> 4 escapes, F5 80 80 80 (>U+10FFFF) -> 4 escapes, F8 88 80 80 80 (5-byte) -> 5 escapes, FE FF -> 2 escapes.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '\\udce2\\udc82A'\n
findings.rule: A truncated sequence terminated by a valid ASCII byte escapes only the incomplete bytes; resynchronisation is immediate. Also: E2 -> '\udce2', E2 82 -> '\udce2\udc82', F0 9F -> '\udcf0\udc9f', F0 9F 98 -> 3 escapes, F0 9F 98 41 -> '\udcf0\udc9f\udc98A', C2 41 -> '\udcc2A'.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: 'A\xc3\xa9\\udcff'\n
findings.rule: Mixed valid/invalid: valid printable non-ASCII is re-emitted as RAW UTF-8 bytes (C3 A9 for e-acute), invalid bytes as literal \udcXX. So stderr is a mix of raw UTF-8 and ASCII escape text in one line.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '\\x01'\n
findings.rule: repr() escaping for control chars: C0 controls other than \t \n \r use \xHH (lowercase hex, 2 digits). Verified \x01, \x1b, \x7f -> '\x01','\x1b','\x7f'.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '\\t'\n
findings.rule: Only TAB/LF/CR get the short forms \t \n \r. NOTE 0x0B and 0x0C are NOT escaped here because int() strips them as whitespace, so '\x0b1' actually PARSES to 1 (rc=0). Whitespace-only stripping accepted by int(): ' 1 ', '\t1', '1\t', '\x0b1', '\x0c1' all succeed.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: 'a\\nb'\n
findings.rule: Embedded newlines in argv can NEVER break stderr into extra lines: repr escapes them. stderr is always exactly 2 lines on the type-error path (wc -l == 2).

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: ''\n
findings.rule: Empty --val gives empty repr ''. Also --val ' ' (single space) -> ' ' — ASCII 0x20 is 'printable' to repr and is NOT escaped, unlike every other Unicode space.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '\\xa0'\n
findings.rule: CRITICAL DISAMBIGUATION: U+00A0 arriving as valid UTF-8 (C2 A0) prints as '\xa0'; the raw byte 0xA0 (invalid UTF-8) prints as '\udca0'. Same for 0xFF vs U+00FF. A port must keep decode-failure and non-printable-codepoint escaping as two separate stages.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '\\u200b'\n
findings.rule: repr escapes non-printable BMP codepoints as \uHHHH (4 lowercase hex). Verified: U+200B '​', U+2028 ' ', U+2029 ' ', U+2000 ' ', U+FEFF '﻿', U+1680 ' ', U+3000 '　', U+F8FF ''. U+00AD -> '\xad', U+0085 -> '\x85' (cp<0x100 uses \xHH).

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '\\U000f0000'\n
findings.rule: Non-printable astral codepoints use \UHHHHHHHH (8 lowercase hex). U+F0000 (Co) -> '\U000f0000'; U+10FFFF (Cn) -> '\U0010ffff'. Printable astral chars are NOT escaped: U+1F600 emoji and U+1D41A both emit raw 4-byte UTF-8.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '\xcc\x81'\n
findings.rule: Combining marks (category Mn) ARE printable to repr and pass through as raw UTF-8. Verified U+0301 (CC 81) and U+0900 (E0 A4 80). Printability rule = codepoint NOT in {Cc,Cf,Cs,Co,Cn,Zl,Zp,Zs}, with ASCII 0x20 forced printable.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: "it's"\n
findings.rule: repr QUOTE SELECTION: if the string contains ' and no ", repr switches to DOUBLE quotes. Verified: "it's", "'" -> "'", 'a\\'b' input a\'b -> "a\\'b".

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: 'both \\' and "'\n
findings.rule: If BOTH quote chars present, repr uses single quotes and backslash-escapes only the single quote. Double quotes are never escaped. Backslash is ALWAYS doubled: input back\slash -> 'back\\slash'.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '  12x  '\n
findings.rule: argparse reprs the ORIGINAL untrimmed argv string, not a normalised form. No truncation, no ellipsis — verified with a 100000-char value producing a 100112-byte stderr.

findings.stderr: usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY --val VAL\ntest6_executable: error: argument --val: invalid int value: '111...1'\n
findings.rule: HARD LIMIT sys.set_int_max_str_digits=4300 (Python 3.12). <=4300 digits parses fine (rc=0); >=4301 digits raises ValueError -> rc=2 with the ENTIRE string echoed (stderr = 4413 bytes for 4301 digits). Count includes leading zeros, EXCLUDES sign and surrounding whitespace: '-'+4301 digits also fails, 4301 zeros fails, 4300 zeros succeeds (value 0). Keep argv as Buffers end-to-end. Fall back to process.argv if /proc is unavailable (non-Linux).

Implement a strict Python UTF-8 decoder with surrogateescape over each argv Buffer, producing a JS string. Rules verified byte-for-byte: accept only minimal-length sequences encoding a scalar in [0,0x10FFFF] excluding D800-DFFF; reject overlong (C0/C1 leads, E0 80-9F, F0 80-8F), surrogate encodings (ED A0-BF), out-of-range (F4 90+, F5-FF), 5/6-byte leads (F8-FD), and stray continuations (80-BF). Build this as a shared decodeArgvBuffer(buf) used for --key, --val, and argv[0].

Implement Python repr(str) exactly for the argparse 'invalid int value: %r' message. Quote choice: default single quotes; if the string contains U+0027 and does NOT contain U+0022, use double quotes; escape U+0027 as \\' only when single-quoted, never escape U+0022. Always escape backslash as \\\\. Short escapes for U+0009 \\t, U+000A \\n, U+000D \\r. Printable == Unicode general category not in {Cc,Cf,Cs,Co,Cn,Zl,Zp,Zs}, with U+0020 forced printable. Iterate by CODEPOINT (for..of / codePointAt), not UTF-16 unit, except that lone surrogates must be handled individually.

You need a printability predicate without npm. Do not try to embed all of Unicode. Practical approach: (1) cp<0x20 or 0x7F<=cp<=0xA0 or cp==0xAD -> not printable; (2) 0xD800<=cp<=0xDFFF -> not printable (lone surrogate); (3) use JS RegExp Unicode property escapes, which Node 18 supports natively: /\p{Cc}|\p{Cf}|\p{Cs}|\p{Co}|\p{Cn}|\p{Zl}|\p{Zp}|\p{Zs}/u tested against the single-codepoint string, with U+0020 special-cased as printable.
